NextItNet’s causal dilated convolutions and residual connections provide architectural routes for historical evidence; accessibility alone does not establish learned use. The [original paper](https://fajieyuan.github.io/papers/nextitnet6.pdf) describes alternative residual blocks, so receptive-field analysis must follow the actual implementation. Enumerate reachable positions through every convolution and skip connection, then compare reachability with measured intervention effects at the final nonpadding readout.

Activation-patching research supports replacing selected internal activations with values from matched clean/corrupted runs. [Zhang and Nanda](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042) show that corruption choices and evaluation metrics can materially change localization results. [Heimersheim and Nanda’s 2024 guidance](https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/FhryNAFknqKAdDcYy/how-to-use-and-interpret-activation-patching) recommends examining both restoration and disruption. A [2025 faithfulness study](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.529.pdf) applies patching to explanation assessment, while [ICLR 2026 work](https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2026/hash/133e588e1429f9f1e25b215da145580e-Abstract-Conference.html) demonstrates that interventions can produce unnatural internal representations. Patching effects therefore need distribution-sensitive controls and cautious interpretation.

Proposed adaptation to the existing NextItNet checkpoint: patch residual-branch outputs at identical sequence positions, separating recent and older history perturbations matched for replacement count and item frequency. Use identity patches, padding controls, and sites with no downstream causal path to the readout; these should have negligible effects. If gates exist, intervene separately on gate values and branch content—small gates alone do not prove useful information is suppressed. Measure target-score margins, rank changes, and recovery/disruption, retaining raw differences when recovery denominators approach zero. Compare attribution rankings against actual intervention effects and random-site controls across users/categories. These are proposed convolution-specific diagnostics, not established findings from the cited language-model studies; they require no additional predictor training.
